## Why you exist

A waiver is the one place in this tool where a PERSON, not a rule, accounts for a line — and it is the one defect class the harness cannot catch for itself. A waiver whose reason sounds plausible and is not true of the lines it covers reads exactly like a correct one: `RESULT: clean`, exit 0, the reason printed back at the reader. Carola (the author) already got one wrong and corrected it herself — BAD-049's `containerMode -> inContainer()`, first waived as "a load-time capture becoming a live read", which was false: old `scripts/web-api.js:151` is `let containerMode = false;`, assigned inside `configure()`, so it was already mutable and already read per request. I have re-verified that correction and it is now right (old 151/156/916 against `072153a:scripts/web-api/seam.js` 26/31/102-103). **One was wrong. Find out whether others are.**

## The job

For every waiver group in all six files, decide whether the reason is TRUE of the lines it signs for. The method is not reading the reason and nodding — it is going to the two revisions and checking. `corpus.json` in the same directory names the old and new revision for each split. Read the old side with `git show '<rev>:<path>'` and the new side with `git show '<rev>:<path>'` or `git ls-tree`; **read-only git only**.

The failure modes to look for, in rough order of how likely they are to be real:

1. **A reason that claims a value or a timing is unchanged when it is not.** The `containerMode` one was this shape. Anything of the form "same value, same timing", "unchanged", "exactly what X returns", "each name is one the old body had in scope" is a checkable claim — check it against the old lines.
2. **A reason narrower than the lines it covers.** A group whose prose describes one line and whose `lines` array holds twelve; or prose that justifies a rewording and covers a line that also changed meaning.
3. **A reason that is true but describes the WRONG old lines.** Reasons cite old line numbers in several places (`old line 916`, `old lines 294-352`, `old 635-686`, `seam.js:26/31/102`). Every citation is checkable; check each one.
4. **A signed line that is not what the reason says it is** — most importantly the two load-bearing ones in `bad-047-collab.json`: the `Room` group's claim that `collab` is handed back BY IDENTITY and never a spread copy (this is BAD-036 risk 6, the bug the whole harness exists to catch — verify it against the landed `c6b41a9:server/supabase/functions/collab/room.ts`), and the `Caller` group's claim that typing `email` honestly "would add two TS2345s that main does not print".
5. **The three destructuring groups in `bad-047-collab.json`** (18 `const { ... } = c;` lines, 12 `const { ... } = r;` lines) are the biggest single risk by volume: each claims "each name is one the old body had in scope at that point". Sample at least six of them and check the named fields against the corresponding old region of `a0baf97:server/supabase/functions/collab/index.ts`. Say how many you checked and which.

## What I need back

A list: for each group, TRUE / FALSE / UNSURE, and for anything not TRUE, the file, the group's reason, the lines, and the old and new lines you read that make it wrong. Quote the `git show` commands you ran. If they are all true, say so plainly and say how many you checked by going to the revisions versus how many you judged from the text alone — that distinction is the whole value of your answer.

Do not fix anything. Do not re-audit the harness code — that is mine and it is done; you are auditing the human claims only.
